Your brain deleted the first three years of your life…
on purpose.
Give me 60 seconds, and I'll show you where those
memories went.
Your first birthday.
Your first steps. Your first word.
Gone.
Scientists call it infantile amnesia.
And everyone has it.
But here's the weird part.
Babies remember just fine.
Three-month-olds can remember a toy for days.
Brain scans show one-year-olds storing memories in the hippocampus, your brain's memory hub.
So what goes wrong?
A baby's brain is a construction site.
It builds over a million new connections every second.
And the hippocampus keeps adding brand new neurons.
Scientists think they wire in…
and scramble the old paths.
Like repaving a road while the cars are still on it.
Plus, you had no words yet.
No words, no story to file it under.
Around age seven, most of what's left fades fast.
And that first memory you think you have?
Almost four in ten people say they remember being two or younger.
Researchers think most of those memories are made up.
But here's the twist.
In mice,
scientists switched forgotten baby memories back on.
So yours might not be gone.
You just lost the key.
